_what: Two knobs for the disk-contention A/B. Edit between runs; the app re-reads this file at the start of every cell alignment, so it does NOT need restarting. Every run logs which combination it used.
_cell_alignment_workers: How many cells to fit at once. null = leave the measured default alone (cpu_count-2, capped at 16 -> 16 on this box). Ingestion on this same storage measured 117.6 MB/s at 12 workers against 66 MB/s at 36, so the interesting direction is DOWN. Currently set to 6 to test whether the GUI's 23 s paints (469 ms of CPU, thread Waiting in the kernel, machine otherwise at 5% CPU and 163 GB free) go away with fewer children.
_child_io_priority: Where pool children sit in the disk queue: 'verylow' (default), 'low', or 'normal' to switch it off. This one is GLOBAL -- it reaches every pool in the app, not just cell alignment -- so do not run an ingestion or a tracing job during an arm.
_the_four_arms: 1. {"cell_alignment_workers": null, "child_io_priority": "normal"}   <- the old behaviour, the control
_reading_the_log: Each run logs one line: settings -> the pool actually built | N passes in T s (rate) | GUI blocked X% of the run, lag median/p95/worst. Compare 'rate' (did the alignment get slower?) against 'blocked %' (did the window get usable?). A run whose pool shape differs from the others -- 'per-hybe' instead of 'across-cells' -- is NOT a comparable arm; that happens when only one cell had work.
